import pytest
from solution import (run, VMError, StackUnderflow, BadJump, BadOpcode,
                      StepLimitExceeded, VMZeroDivision)


def test_neg_comparisons():
    assert run([("PUSH", 3), ("NEG",)]) == [-3]
    assert run([("PUSH", 2), ("PUSH", 2), ("EQ",)]) == [1]
    assert run([("PUSH", 1), ("PUSH", 2), ("LT",)]) == [1]
    assert run([("PUSH", 1), ("PUSH", 2), ("GT",)]) == [0]


def test_div_mod_zero():
    with pytest.raises(VMZeroDivision):
        run([("PUSH", 1), ("PUSH", 0), ("DIV",)])
    with pytest.raises(VMZeroDivision):
        run([("PUSH", 1), ("PUSH", 0), ("MOD",)])


def test_countdown_loop():
    # store[0]=5; loop: load, jz end, load, push 1, sub, store, jmp loop; end
    prog = [("PUSH", 5), ("STORE", 0),
            ("LOAD", 0), ("JZ", 9),
            ("LOAD", 0), ("PUSH", 1), ("SUB",), ("STORE", 0),
            ("JMP", 2),
            ("LOAD", 0)]
    assert run(prog) == [0]

content.text: The visible suite now passes (3 passed). I changed only `solution/core.py`. The cause was operand order in `run()`. The binary-op branch did `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which bound `a` to the top of the stack, the right-hand operand. So SUB, DIV, MOD, LT and GT all computed right-minus-left or right-compared-to-left. That made `1 < 2` evaluate to 0, let `DIV`/`MOD` check the wrong operand for zero, and broke the countdown loop's `SUB`, so it never reached zero and hit the step limit. I changed the pop to `b, a = pop(), pop()` so `a` is the left operand. I also fixed `SWAP`, which had the same ordering mistake and was effectively a no-op; it now pushes the top value first, so the two values actually swap. I did not touch `tests/`, add dependencies, or change the public API. I did not run the hidden suite, so the fix is verified only against the visible tests.

result: The visible suite now passes (3 passed). I changed only `solution/core.py`. The cause was operand order in `run()`. The binary-op branch did `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which bound `a` to the top of the stack, the right-hand operand. So SUB, DIV, MOD, LT and GT all computed right-minus-left or right-compared-to-left. That made `1 < 2` evaluate to 0, let `DIV`/`MOD` check the wrong operand for zero, and broke the countdown loop's `SUB`, so it never reached zero and hit the step limit. I changed the pop to `b, a = pop(), pop()` so `a` is the left operand. I also fixed `SWAP`, which had the same ordering mistake and was effectively a no-op; it now pushes the top value first, so the two values actually swap. I did not touch `tests/`, add dependencies, or change the public API. I did not run the hidden suite, so the fix is verified only against the visible tests.
